# Clean architecture

This directory is the starting point for the new Hivemind architecture on the `clean-arch` branch.

Read [PRD.md](PRD.md) for the source, or open [architecture.html](architecture.html) for the reading page. The PRD is the single source of truth for the architecture being developed here. The [reference diagram](reference-diagram.png) is Alex's starting picture; where a label on the picture conflicts with the clarified flow in the PRD, the PRD states the clarification. The diagram is a reference image, not an implementation or an acceptance result.

The PRD is a working draft. Its open questions and untested choices must not be mistaken for approved implementation contracts. Two parts are decided: Step 1 runs the adopted request c8 (D387, closed by D391), and Step 2 with Step 3's grouping library is frozen (D427; `tests/test_frozen_clean_step2.py`). Step 4 is in progress. Nothing here is integrated with production storage; the clean path goes to production as a whole, after Step 4 meets its lines. The existing product and historical research are separate from this draft and remain available for reference.

After editing `PRD.md`, run `node clean-arch/render.mjs` from the repository root. Run `node clean-arch/render.mjs --check` to verify that the HTML matches the source. The repository's `python3 docs/check.py` also runs this check. The HTML is generated; do not edit it by hand. The renderer uses the repository's existing Markdown renderer and Node.js.

# Where the clean path stands: progress and results, for the council (2026-11-12)

Written at Alex's request ("你能先准备搞一个段落让整个council看一下你的过去跑的整体进度和反馈结果吗？我们到底做到哪里了") before
Stage B is sent. Every number points to the page that holds it; where I give a view, it is labelled as mine.

## The goal

A system that reads the day's news on a company, opens the questions an analyst would bet on, files evidence under them and
judges each question every day, at least as well as production does on the frozen ruler (AGENTS §7.1). The clean path rebuilds
this in four steps: Step 1 reads an article and proposes theses and evidence; Step 2 groups repeats and revisions and finds the
right thesis; Step 3 writes the library; Step 4 turns each new thesis into a judged question (the "ladder step") and lets
production's frozen judge judge it daily. Production keeps running until the whole clean path beats it end to end (D427).

## What is done, step by step

| step | state | the numbers that say so | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 extraction | closed on configuration c8 (D387, D391) | — | clean-arch PRD §12; round log §59 |
| 2 search and grouping | closed and frozen; goes to production only with the whole path (D427) | — | Step 2 log §§14–19 |
| 1–3 end to end, seeded with the ruler's 22 questions | **inconclusive** under its frozen rule (q12 0 of 3) | judged answers agreeing with the gold: clean 18, 18, 17 against production 17, 15, 16 (three draws each); conditional on the supplied questions, on articles c8 was tuned on (115 of 243); capital spending (q12) a known gap (D394) | D392, D393, D394; round log §63 |
| 1–3 end to end, unseeded (the system opens its own questions) | behind | graded subset 4.0 against 6.33 seeded (a different day, exploratory); all questions 6, 5, 5 against 18, 18, 17, mostly company-figure questions the product does not open (D370); every graded miss a question not opened in the ruler's shape | D395; `unseeded-2026-11-10/` |
| 4a the ladder step | built; measured four times; **has not passed Alex's lines**; frozen as it ran in the fourth measurement (D426) | below | `step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/result-*/RESULT.md` |
| 4b the frozen judge on the ladder step's questions (Stage B) | built and reviewed twice; not yet sent | below | `step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/` |

## Step 4a: the ladder step, four measurements (Stage A: 44 stored theses, three sends each; lines D400)

| line (D400) | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | run 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 no ladder asks another question | missed | missed | missed | missed by 1 (agreed rulings) |
| 2 no part left unlisted | missed | missed | missed | **met** |
| 3 no outcome with no rung or two | missed | missed | missed | missed by 2 |
| 4 no unjustified refusal | missed | missed | met on lenient readings | missed by 3 |
| 5 ≥35 of 44 right in 2 of 3 sends, ≥28 by a ladder | missed | missed | met on lenient readings | met on two of three readings |
| 6 same favourable end; same due day ≥ 9 in 10 | missed | missed (due day 18 of 34) | **met** | **met** (33 of 33) |

Between runs, each change came from Alex's rulings on what the readers disputed (D409–D421), each tested alone on a few stored
cases before it went in; several went into one run together, so which change fixed what rests on the small probes. Each run
showed a new small class; run 3 went back on lines 1 and 2. **The table above gives the strict reading; on "both first readers
fail", run 1 missed lines 3, 4 and 6, run 4 lines 3 and 4, and line 3 fell from 7 failures to 1.** Line 6 is met by
construction once code sets the due day (D414). A "second look" (the
model re-checking its own answer) was tested and did not pass: 6 of 18 agreed faults mended (9 needed), 3 of 30 sound answers
damaged (D422, D425). Alex then froze the step (D426): no more tuning on these 44 theses. Spent: about $1.25 of D401's $3.

What is still wrong in the step as frozen, from run 4's agreed rulings: a Kyber question written "during calendar 2027" with a
due day at the end of 2028; a "restructuring" counted as a deal being off; three refusals for "two figures, none the main one";
eight theses of 34 in the unseeded draws get no question at all, and the evidence later filed to them (200 links in the dry
runs) goes nowhere.

## Step 4b: the frozen judge, the baseline reading done, the system's own questions not yet run

- **Baseline (D426):** the frozen judge on the ruler's hand-written ladders, 159 stored judgements read by two reader families
  (Codex, Claude Opus 5.5) after seven reviews of the reading plan, with six planted wrong answers (all caught by both
  families, the stored rung named). Result: **4 of 151 decided judgements unsupported (3%), all in figure questions (4 of 52,
  8%); yes/no 0 of 99; 16 of 16 questions end the window on a supported judgement.** Every fault is in three figure questions
  before any amount is in the evidence: the judge picks the lowest rung for want of a number, or reaches for a number the
  evidence does not give (`stage_b/RESULT.md`).
- **Lines for Stage B (D428):** figure and yes/no compared apart: figure judgements unsupported at most 5 points above the
  baseline (12.7% to 14.4%), yes/no at most 5%, last judgements at most one in ten unsupported; plus the design's completeness,
  coverage and control lines; the control rule settled before the send (D430). Their chance behaviour is measured: a figure line
  five points above baseline is crossed by chance 6% to 17% with an unchanged judge (`stage_b/result/line-chance.txt`).
- **The run (D429):** the adapter's ladder mode is built (`stage_b/ladder_adapter.py`, `run_stage_b.py`; 19 tests; 13 mutants
  each caught by its own test; dry runs at $0: 26 of 26 laddered views written and judged, 236 judgements; 159 real stored
  judge answers pass the judge's own check). Two fresh reviews found it not ready (the $2 cap could be passed by a redo or a
  second launch; a view opened already due could be judged; provenance and counts); all changed. A third review is next;
  then three draws, about $0.45 estimated, cap $2.

## How the work has gone (my reading, for the council to challenge)

- **The measuring took more rounds than the building.** The baseline's reading plan needed seven reviews before readers
  started; twice the same finding came back and was closed only by changing the mechanism (every judgement read alone; a
  planted answer used only after a trial). The Stage B build needed three. Each review found real defects (a cap that could
  be passed; controls a reader could pick out), so I do not count them as wasted, but the pace is slow.
- **The readers are the instrument and the instrument moves.** In Stage A the two third readers agreed on 21 of 70 points
  (runs 2, 3) and 29 of 53 (run 4); fresh readers re-reading run 4's answers agreed again on 14 of its 18 agreed faults. In
  the baseline the families agreed on 155 of 159, which shows agreement, not calibration: no control is known to be sound.
- **The ladder step's remaining faults are few but not scattered** (corrected by the council): five of the six answers behind
  lines 1, 3 and 4 sit on theses whose outcome names two things or two periods, which is how Step 1 cut them.
- **Where I was wrong, recorded:** predictions made from one judgement or one skim were wrong several times (a financing
  question I expected to stay unsupported; a "7 of 18 mended" count before the readers); a reviewer started with write access
  once (stopped in a minute, no file changed); a check of mine stricter than the form refused seven correct rows (corrected
  before the count).

## Distance to production (my reading)

Not close, and no date can be given from this record. In order:
1. Stage B: send, read (about 236 judgements, two families, controls), judge against D428 and D430.
2. If Stage B passes: the clean path end to end against production on the frozen ruler, three draws each (D427). The
   unseeded opening gap (4.0 against 6.33) and capital spending (q12) are the known reasons it could lose there.
3. The real search and save path, integration, and the end-to-end acceptance before production is replaced.
If Stage B fails: the faults it finds are diagnosed to the step that causes them (ladder step, judge, or the questions Step 1
opens) before anything changes.

## The council's read (2026-11-12)

Two independent members checked this page against the record; their corrections are applied above and their consensus is
`clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/council/kr-consensus.md`: the numbers hold, the emphasis was too favourable in four places;
the next step is Stage B; the largest demonstrated gap is upstream, in how Step 1 cuts a matter into theses; and two decisions
are Alex's: the end-to-end yardstick for D427 and whether a Stage B pass counts as Step 4 meeting its lines.

# Stage B result: the frozen judge on the ladder step's own questions (2026-11-12)

**Stage B does not pass.** Line 3, the control theses, is unexercised: 4 controls are eligible with reader B's material shown,
fewer than the 8 the design requires ("else the control is unexercised and Stage B cannot pass"). The four agree with reader B.
On the judgements themselves, lines 1 and 2 and the figure and yes/no lines are met on all three readings; the last-judgement
line is met on two readings and missed on the strictest (3 of 24 when unresolved verdicts count as UNSUPPORTED). **Stage A has
not passed** (D426); nothing here changes that.

Run: three draws, 236 judgements, $0.4161 (`poc/data/clean-stage-b-2026-11-11/`). Reading: `poc/data/clean-stage-b-reading-2026-11-12/`
(the plan `STAGE_B_READING.md`, reviewed five times, `council/kv`–`kz`). Counts: `result/stage-b-count.txt`, `result/control-count.txt`.

## The lines (D428, D430; the design's §8)

| line | result |
|---|---|
| 1, no draw incomplete | met |
| 2, nine in ten laddered theses judged | met: 26 of 26 (u1 9 of 9, u2 8 of 8, u3 9 of 9) |
| 3, control theses | **unexercised**: eligible 7 (literal reading 4); with reader B's material shown 4, all 4 agreeing; fewer than 8 |
| figure, UNSUPPORTED at most baseline + 5 points | met: 3/88 (3.4%) against 12.7%; 3/95 (3.2%) against 12.5%; 10/95 (10.5%) against 14.4% |
| yes/no, UNSUPPORTED at most 5% | met: 1/117 (0.9%); 1/122 (0.8%); 6/122 (4.9%, at the line) |
| last judgements, at most one in ten UNSUPPORTED | met 0/21, met 0/24, **missed 3/24 (12.5%)** on the strictest reading; INSUFFICIENT 2 beside |

The three readings are: unresolved left out; unresolved counted SUPPORTED; unresolved counted UNSUPPORTED.

## The controls of the reading

- Trial: all six planted answers passed (both families UNSUPPORTED with the stored rung named), covering the three tests.
- Reading: both families caught 6 of 6 planted answers, naming the stored rung. Repeats: two read the same by both families;
  one (u2 v5 #5) read UNSUPPORTED both times by Codex and SUPPORTED both times by Claude, consistent within each family.
- The families differ on 22 of 236 stored judgements (9%; the void line is a third). Both third readers ruled each; they agreed
  on 10 and split on 12. On 9 of the 12 each third reader sided with its own family's first reader; on 3 (u1 v8 #4, u2 v5 #2,
  #4) each sided with the other family's (the council-loop skill's trap, "model readers carry their family's threshold", holds
  for most of the splits).
- Hours: Codex 0.3, Claude 2.4 (estimate 3.5 each). Codex reads with few visible reasoning tokens, as in the baseline (same
  setting, comparable). Three Claude sessions reported one shell command each on their own packet (a size check, a grep);
  none opened another file; their rows are kept and disclosed (`stage-b-reading-claude-sessions-notes.md`).

## Against the baseline (the frozen judge on hand-written ladders)

| | baseline (159) | Stage B (236) |
|---|---|---|
| figure UNSUPPORTED, unresolved left out | 4/52 (7.7%) | 3/88 (3.4%) |
| yes/no UNSUPPORTED, unresolved left out | 0/99 | 1/117 |
| INSUFFICIENT | 7 | 19, all figure questions |
| unresolved | 1 | 12 |
| all UNSUPPORTED, unresolved counted UNSUPPORTED | 5/152 (3.3%) | 16/217 (7.4%) |
| last judgements | 16 of 16 SUPPORTED | 21 of 26 SUPPORTED, 3 unresolved, 2 INSUFFICIENT |

With the unresolved left out or counted SUPPORTED, Stage B's UNSUPPORTED share is no higher than the baseline's; counted
UNSUPPORTED, it is higher overall (7.4% against 3.3%), though the figure and yes/no lines Alex set are each still met (council B,
`council/la-codex.md`). Its INSUFFICIENT and unresolved verdicts are higher on every reading. A share no worse than the
baseline's would not show the ladders sound (the plan's limits).

## What the traces show (my own read of all 17 judgements a reader calls UNSUPPORTED, and the INSUFFICIENT clusters)

The disputed and INSUFFICIENT verdicts sit on eight of the 26 questions (five matters, some asked in more than one draw), in
three patterns. Council B read two judgements of each and found the patterns real; the right rung in the disputed cases is not
established:

1. **"Still open" chosen because nothing is settled yet (Kyber, u1 v6 and u2 v5; 7 judgements).** The ladder step writes an
   event in three outcomes (Yes, Ruled out, Still open). The judge keeps "Still open" because neither a shipment nor a formal
   delay is established today, which its own rules forbid ("'not established' is a statement of confidence, never a reason to
   stay"). On the due day "Still open" needs NVIDIA silent about a slip for a whole year, the least likely outcome. The
   baseline's events had two outcomes, so this could not happen there. u1 v6 also carries a ladder defect Stage A recorded: a
   "during calendar 2027" event due 2028-12-31. The faulty reason is real; the right rung is not settled: a reported 2028
   shipment does not establish that NVIDIA will make the formal announcement "Ruled out" needs. My read is UNSUPPORTED on all
   seven; the families split and the third readers split, so these are my reading, not seven settled errors.
2. **Figure questions the evidence cannot size (u1 v1, u3 v1, u1 v8, u2 v7, u3 v10; 19 INSUFFICIENT).** The questions opened
   with no reference figure ("no reference figure when the question opened") and, in the INSUFFICIENT judgements, the evidence
   shown holds no comparable: NVIDIA's credit support to cloud partners (later judgements do use a disclosed backstop as a
   comparable), the hyperscalers' custom-chip revenue (which is not broken out in the evidence shown), HBM wafer capacity added
   in 2027. The judge picks a range anyway; readers call it INSUFFICIENT. The 19 repeat a few questions day after day.
3. **A figure carried forward instead of re-derived (u2 v7, $28bn of custom-accelerator spend; u3 v8, supply commitments).**
   u2 v7 keeps $28bn without deriving it, beside Broadcom's AI revenue ($10.8bn a quarter, $16bn guided), which the evidence does
   not split by buyer; my read that a share of it crosses $30bn adds an assumption the evidence does not hold. u3 v8 keeps $119bn
   flat, then scales it by revenue growth to rung 5; the evidence shown does not establish that commitments move with revenue,
   and readers, third readers and I disagree on whether that scaling is allowed. Neither alternative figure is established.

## Line 3, what failed

Of the 16 controls, the Ohio question is listed apart. Of the other 15:
- **8 are not eligible on the question**: 6 are not the same question as the ruler's (both readers, or both third readers on
  u2/clean-3), and on 2 the third readers split (u1/clean-6, which also has another due day, and u1/clean-11). The judged
  question asks about another quantity, scope or period than the hand-written ruler question. **Where that difference is made
  is not yet traced** (council B): the matching rule that paired them deliberately counts a part of a total, or the same event
  under another deadline, as the same matter (`unseeded-2026-11-10/MATCHING-v2.md`), and the ladder step writes the judged
  question and due day after Step 1, so the difference may come from Step 1, from the ladder step, or from the pairing's breadth. This is how Step 1 cuts a
  matter into theses: the diagnosis Alex chose next (D432).
- Of the 7 eligible, **3 had part of reader B's decisive material not shown to the judge** by 2026-07-14 (u1/clean-4 and
  u3/clean-6, q13; u2/clean-4, q04); where it was lost (linked and not shown, or never linked) is not yet traced.
- The 4 with the material shown all agree with reader B.
- **The trace (done, `CONTROL_TRACE.md`, checked by `council/lb-codex.md`):** most question differences are already in the
  Step 1 thesis (a programme inside a total, the article's reported date, a later milestone), kept by the ladder step; one is the
  ladder's wording and one is both. Two controls miss exact statements Step 1 stored with no link to any thesis (a supplier's
  growth forecast, the memory share of spending), though the capex thesis was open; the third missing statement left no record.
  These are leads for the Step 1 diagnosis (D432), not an established attribution.

## Limits

One send of three draws; daily judgements repeat questions (236 are not 236 independent tests); the planted answers are plain
errors; the third readers split by family on 12, so the strict readings move with that split; the control count compares 4
cases. Stage A has not passed.

stored seeded draws already agree with the frozen reference on 15, 15 and 16 of 17 questions; the rebuild and dry-run harness

The cold reflection council asked for by D542 is complete (`research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-2/`: Claude's reflection
written first, a fresh independent reading of the whole record, one challenge round, consensus). **No investigation is open.**
D518 stands with its reasons made explicit: the old system stays the default and both systems stay, for continuity and because
the new system's answer-choice step has not passed its tests and it is not integrated with production storage; **the quality of
the two systems' answers is not ranked, and the council does not make the choice in Alex's place.** Why nothing is opened

# The new system's position, and the choices left (D477), 2026-11-13

**In one line:** the new system is not ready to replace the current one, and further wording fixes on this test set no longer move it; what
is left are choices about how the product is built. (Checked by the council, round 23.)

## Where it stands

- **The step that writes each question's answer options**, on 40 questions, must get at least 26 right with options it wrote (scaled from your
  line of 28 of 44). It gets 22. Of the other 18, 10 are declines that the readers count as right, and 8 are wrong.
- **Why it declines (the 11 declines its first pass made, checked by two independent readers):** six are right, and four of those six are
  questions the first step should never have opened (a stake already completed, a $500 million stake too small to matter, a background
  sentence, a figure no public report will settle). In four, the article supports a question worth asking that could be given options: the
  H100 rental price twice (the step sometimes files it under the semiconductor-cycle topic and sometimes says no topic covers it) and the
  memory price twice (once the first step wrote "the 12 months to mid-2027" instead of one calendar year; once it tied the price to a bank's
  estimate of one rack's memory cost). On paper, fixing all four and losing nothing would give 26. That is arithmetic, not an expected result:
  the readers did not check that the replacement questions would get good options, and they are narrower than the originals.
- **What today's fixes did:** four wording changes to the first step (the year split, the identity rule, the calendar-year rule, the
  unsigned-deal rule) were tested, on stored articles and, for two of them, on unseen ones. None was adopted: each moved the error to a
  neighbouring question, made the model stop asking, or found the old version already doing it half the time. The model's answers to the same
  request also swing widely (one question opened 3 of 3 times in one test and 0 of 3 in another), so three tries per case cannot show small
  gains.
- **Spend:** about $27 of the $40 ceiling I set myself for this period; nothing committed or pushed.

## The choices

1. **Define the research topics more fully.** The list of world topics (`poc/universe.json`, shared with the current system) defines
   "semiconductor cycle" only by industry revenue growth. The model files memory prices under it every time; it filed the H100 rental price
   under it in 3 of 9 tries, under a wrong topic once, and declined 5 times. Naming what each topic carries might settle this; that is untested.
   Where the H100 question did get options, 20 later judgements referred to it and one said it pushed the other way "but not enough" to change
   its answer; whether it changes any final answer is unmeasured.
2. **Make the first step write the answer options itself**, so that a question it cannot give options to is, in intention, not opened in that
   shape. Untested. It could touch at most the two memory cases and the over-opened questions, not the H100 declines unless the topic rule also
   changes; like two earlier attempts, it may make the model stop opening hard questions. Its benefit, risk and cost would be designed and
   reviewed before any send.
3. **Put the effort back into the current system.** It stays the default either way; the new system's parts (search, comparison, grouping)
   remain built and frozen for later.

The council has made no choice among these: D477 records them for you and stops paid tests on the new system until a choice is made by you,
or by the council on new evidence.

# Are the eleven first-pass refusals reachable? Two blind readers, $0 (D476), 2026-11-13

**Answer: of the eleven theses the judge's first pass refused on the full run, both readers agree on ten. Six should be declined: no
question worth asking in any shape the ladder step can take (five distinct matters). Four runs, two distinct matters, have a question
worth asking that the article supports in a shape that can be laddered: the H100 rental price (twice, from one article) and the memory
price (two articles). They split on one: federal AI obligations.** On this population Stage A counts 32 right, 22 by a written ladder,
of 40 (line scaled to 32 and 26). So the written line is reachable on paper only if all four agreed conversions land and nothing else is
lost: +4 gives 26.

Readers: Codex (`codex-phase1.jsonl`, `codex-phase2.jsonl`) and a Claude subagent (`claude-phase1.jsonl`, `claude-phase2.jsonl`). Each read

**I choose the new system as the path for work toward production.** The old system remains the running default until the new system passes its gates. Both remain available, and this decision does not establish that the new system’s answers are better.

I accept your correction to our earlier consensus: D439 gives the council the job of taking a course. We treated an inconclusive comparison as a reason to leave that course undecided.

The reason I choose the rebuild is that Alex had already reopened work on it, and its treatment of the company’s financial figures follows the product direction he most recently confirmed. The fresh week gives no demonstrated reason to abandon it. It also shows fewer trivial or duplicate questions in that one run. Those observations support continuing the rebuild; they do not prove it will be the better system.

I would qualify two parts of your argument:

- The old system’s coverage advantage comes from financial questions Alex ruled out **for the new system**. The record still lists whether that rule applies to the old system as an open choice. We should not claim he already decided it for both.
- The new system is reversible as a **work decision**, but its cost and time to reach production are unknown.
